question: What does the acronym 'ASCII' stand for in computer terminology?

options.text: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
American Scientific Code for Information Interchange
Advanced Standard Code for Information Interchange
American Standard Code for International Interchange

solution:
The correct answer is __**American Standard Code for Information Interchange**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ASCII** stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**, which is a character encoding standard used in computers and other electronic devices for representing text.
 
• It was first developed in the **1960s** by the American National Standards Institute (**ANSI**) to standardize text representation across different platforms and devices.
 
• **ASCII** uses a 7-bit binary code to represent **128 unique characters**, including uppercase and lowercase letters, digits, punctuation marks, and special control characters like newline or tab.
 
• The standard is widely used in programming, data communication, and text files, as it ensures compatibility between systems.
 
• **Extended ASCII** variants expand the character set to **256 characters** by using 8 bits, enabling support for additional symbols and language-specific characters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Development of ASCII:**

 
 
• **ASCII** was developed by a committee led by Robert W. Bemer in the early 1960s to create a standard for encoding text in digital systems.
 
• It was approved in 1963 and revised in **1967** to include the lowercase alphabet and additional symbols.
 
 
 
• **Applications of ASCII:**
 
 
• Widely used in **programming languages** like C and Python for text processing.
 
• Essential in **internet protocols** like HTTP, SMTP, and FTP for communication between systems.
 
• Used in **plain text files** (.txt) and in encoding data for transfer between different platforms.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of ASCII:**
 
 
• Uses a **7-bit binary representation**, allowing 128 unique character codes.
 
• Includes printable characters like letters, digits, and symbols, as well as control characters like **line feed** and **carriage return**.
 
• It is **platform-independent**, making it ideal for cross-platform compatibility.
 
 
 
• **Extended ASCII and Unicode:**
 
 
• **Extended ASCII** uses 8 bits to represent 256 characters, adding support for language-specific characters and symbols.
 
• **Unicode** is a modern standard that builds upon ASCII, supporting over **143,000 characters** from various scripts and symbols worldwide.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Control Characters:**

 
 
• ASCII includes control characters like **NULL (0)**, **Start of Header (SOH)**, and **End of Transmission (EOT)**, which are used in data communication.
 
• These characters are non-printable and are used for signaling and formatting.
 
 
 
• **ASCII Table:**
 
 
• The **ASCII table** maps characters to their corresponding decimal, hexadecimal, and binary codes.
 
• For example, the letter **'A'** corresponds to **65 (decimal)** or **01000001 (binary)**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy and Compatibility:**
 
 
• Despite the rise of Unicode, ASCII remains widely used in legacy systems and for basic text processing.
 
• Its simplicity and universal adoption make it a foundational standard in computing.
